title: Evaluating a Piecewise Rule at a Negative Input
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Let $f(x)=x+2$ when $x<0$ and $f(x)=x^{2}$ when $x\ge 0$. Find $f(-3)$, saying which branch supplies the answer.

steps.title: Test the Input Against the Conditions
steps.explanation: The input $-3$ is negative, so the linear branch governs; the quadratic branch never sees it.
steps.why: Piecewise evaluation always begins by checking which condition the input satisfies.

steps.title: Apply the Selected Rule
steps.why: Only one formula is active at a time, so the arithmetic is ordinary.

steps.title: Sanity Check the Branch Choice
steps.explanation: Plugging $-3$ into $x^2$ would be illegal here because that branch is reserved for $x\\ge 0$.
steps.why: A classic error is using the wrong piece; the domain tags must be respected.
